category_title: Low-achieving students in inclusive settings who exhibit superficial responses or off-task behavior when objectives are unclear
minimal_context: The student is working on an anticipation-reaction guide and examining photographs and resource maps of different countries in the classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Okay, look at your anticipation-reaction guides. For each statement, you need to check 'Agree' or 'Disagree' based on the photographs and resource maps.

STUDENT: Are we supposed to write that down? We don't have nothin' in the box right here.

TUTOR: No, if you need to write something, write it on the back. Let's look at the pictures of the countries.

STUDENT: We have a lot of stuff in this one. That one's clean. The other ones, they're wiggity-wack. Jobs don't pay as much.

TUTOR: Okay, look at number 2 on your guide.

STUDENT: So, what is it? We don't know. It's like court. (The student mouths and pantomimes a debate)

options.A: Allow the student to work on the guide at their own pace and take a break whenever desired.
options.B: Follow through to ensure the student complies with the direction to look at the guide, assisting if needed.
options.C: State the objective in language the student can understand and point to it on the board.
options.D: Lead short practices with an initial focus on breath awareness, belly breathing, and awareness of the body and sounds.
